description: CRIT-004 (line 61) and CRIT-008 (line 143) both declare `dimension: regression_safety` in the contract's YAML frontmatter. 'regression_safety' is not one of the 5 canonical review dimensions this VCSDD process organizes verdicts and convergence signals around -- this review's own input manifest.json explicitly enumerates exactly ['spec_fidelity', 'edge_case_coverage', 'implementation_correctness', 'structural_integrity', 'verification_readiness'] as `reviewDimensions` (manifest.json:28-34), and the adversary role definition uses the same 5-dimension taxonomy for every verdict.json output. Because 2 of the 8 CRIT items are labeled with an undefined 6th dimension, there is no defined rule for which of the 5 official dimensions their PASS/FAIL should roll up into during Phase 3's verdict aggregation or Phase 6's convergence-signal computation -- a downstream aggregator has to silently invent a mapping (as this review itself had to do), which is exactly the kind of interpretive slack a strict-mode contract should not leave open.

evidence.snippet:
- id: CRIT-004
    dimension: regression_safety
    ...
  - id: CRIT-008
    dimension: regression_safety

recommendation: Re-label CRIT-004 and CRIT-008's `dimension` field to one of the 5 canonical values (both are naturally `spec_fidelity`, since they are regression-preservation checks against already-approved REQ-103/REQ-302 acceptance criteria, not a distinct taxonomy of their own).
